text:
kevin: Quick run: comparing prefill-heavy KV sizing vs on-demand (decode-time) caching with a per-request cap. Observed odd tradeoffs — p99 went down in one config but p50 shifted up. Posting configs + numbers.

ash: Can you drop the run config and hardware?

kevin: Sure. Ran on 1xA10x4 equivalent node (4xA10 sim), model: opt-6.7b-like, seq dist: mean 256, tail 1024, batch heuristic: adaptive-batch-v3, kernel_selection: auto, but forced fused-attn-v2 for the second run. Key flags:
```
kv_prefill: true  # experiment A
per_request_kv_cap_mb: 48
allocator.slab_base_mb: 64
allocator.coalesce: false
workspace_reuse: false
adaptive_prefill: false
```
```
kv_prefill: false # experiment B (on-demand)
per_request_kv_cap_mb: 48
allocator.slab_base_mb: 32
allocator.coalesce: true
workspace_reuse: true
adaptive_prefill: false
```

kevin: Short results (100k requests synthetic mix, cold start warmed):
- A (prefill=true): avg GPU mem 5.6GB, frag=13%, throughput=470 r/s, p50=78ms, p95=210ms, p99=232ms, OOMs=0
- B (prefill=false): avg GPU mem 4.9GB, frag=6%, throughput=510 r/s, p50=70ms, p95=215ms, p99=245ms, OOMs=0

priya: Interesting — prefill gives slightly better p99 but worse p50 and fragmentation. Where are the extra cycles going?

kevin: Traces show prefill reduces per-request decode time (less KV misses) but increases allocator churn because we pre-allocate many KV slabs up front; slab fragmentation goes up, causing small allocs during batching windows to fall back to slower paths. Also kernel selection change (fused-attn-v2) increased temporary workspace need by ~8% which made the allocator more sensitive.

leo: Do you have a flamegraph/profile for a p95 vs p99 sample?

kevin: Pasted short profile (top lines):
```
CPU: batching_scheduler::enqueue 22%
GPU memcpy: 18%
allocator::alloc_slab 15%
kv_cache::prefill_upload 12%
kernel_launch::fused_attn_v2 9%
decode::kv_lookup 6%
```
This is for prefill=true. For on-demand, allocator::alloc_slab drops to 5% but decode::kv_lookup rises to 15%.

ash: So the tradeoff is allocator activity vs decode time. Which affects tail depending on batching variance.

kevin: Exactly. I tried an adaptive_prefill prototype: prefill only if request prefix hit rate > 0.6 (estimated from recent windows), otherwise lazy decode. Config: adaptive_prefill=true, prefill_threshold=0.6, slab_base_mb=48, coalesce=true, workspace_reuse=true. Results: avg mem 5.1GB, frag=7%, throughput=500 r/s, p50=72ms, p95=208ms, p99=226ms. Tail improved vs raw on-demand and fragmentation dropped vs full prefill.

priya: Nice. What about per-request caps? Is 48MB the sweet spot?

kevin: I swept caps: 32/48/64MB. 32MB -> lower mem but higher p99 for long context requests (prefill truncation), 64MB -> slightly better tail but fragmentation up ~3pp and throughput down ~5%. 48MB seems a good middle.

leo: Were you running same kernel selection in all cap sweeps?

kevin: Yes except I also tried forcing fused-attn-v1 vs v2. Forcing v2 without bumping slab_base caused up to 6% p99 regression due to workspace spikes. After increasing slab_base_mb and enabling workspace_reuse, regression disappears.

ash: Actionable ops then: 1) enable adaptive_prefill in experiment cluster, 2) tune allocator.slab_base to match chosen kernel (v2 needs +25% base), 3) keep per-request cap at 48MB as default but expose override, 4) enable allocator.coalesce + workspace_reuse by default.

kevin: Agreed. Also adding a perf regression test: when changing kernel_selection we should run a 10k request smoke with current adaptive_prefill + slab settings to detect workspace-related tail regressions. The kernel change yesterday (auto->fused-attn-v2) is what revealed this.

infra-bot: deploy-log: started job perf/kv-prefill-sweep on cluster perf-sim-04 at 2003123490 by kevin

priya: I'll own the rollout checklist. Plan: run 24h burn with production traffic replay, if p99 stays within -2% of baseline and OOMs=0, we flip flag in canary.

leo: One more idea — track fragmentation metric per-GPU over time and trigger slab_compact job when frag > 12% for 5m. Could avoid manual intervention.

kevin: Good. I'll add frag metric to the console dashboard and a small compaction job prototype. Also add a note in the kernel onboarding doc that fused-attn-v2 increases workspace peak and to coordinate with runtime when enabling.

ash: Thanks. Can you drop the perf logs + config in the perf-run bucket and link here?

kevin: Uploaded to s3://perf-runs/kv-prefill-adaptive/2003123456.tar.gz — includes traces, profiles, and the simple adaptive_prefill toggle code.

priya: Cool. I'll take the canary and checklist.

kevin: TL;DR: prefill reduces decode hits but increases allocator churn/fragmentation; on-demand saves mem but can raise tail due to decode spikes. Adaptive prefill + allocator tuning (slab base, coalesce, workspace reuse) gives best overall tradeoff. Next: 24h replay and automated frag-based compaction.
